input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.2 imposes a liquidated exit charge payable by us (the Company) to HDI whenever we terminate, calculated as 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000. That is a customer-payable liquidated amount, contrary to the preferred position, and it fails the fallback by a wide margin: our fees are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month, so the formula can exceed a full year of fees (and far exceeds three months' fees) at any meaningful sales volume. It is also triggered by ordinary 90-day non-renewal under Section 4.1, not just early exit. We propose deleting the Termination Payment and, if an exit charge is unavoidable, capping it at three months' fees.

proposal.summary: Delete the Company-payable Termination Payment in Section 4.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the Termination Payment, as our playbook does not accept liquidated damages or early-termination penalties payable by us, and a charge equal to half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000 would dwarf the fees actually at stake and would apply even on ordinary non-renewal. If an exit charge is essential to HDI, we can discuss one capped at three months' fees.
